title: The Gospel of Mary
author: Christopher Tuckett
description: The Gospel of Mary by Christopher Tuckett (Oxford University Press, 2007, Oxford Early Christian Gospel Texts series), the standard scholarly edition of this second-century text. The Gospel of Mary survives incompletely in a fifth-century Coptic manuscript (Berlin Codex 8502) and two third-century Greek fragments from Oxyrhynchus. In it the risen Saviour teaches about matter and sin, then departs. Mary Magdalene comforts the grieving disciples and relates a private vision describing the soul's ascent past four hostile powers, after which Peter and Andrew challenge her authority and Levi defends her. Tuckett provides an introduction on manuscripts, date, genre and theology, the Coptic and Greek texts with facing English translation, and a detailed commentary, assessing the text's relation to the New Testament and to Gnostic thought and its significance for debates about Mary Magdalene and women's leadership in early Christianity.
